name: DE/rand/1/bin
tagline: Classic differential evolution with rand/1 mutation, binomial crossover, and greedy parent-vs-trial selection.
pseudocode:
1. Initialize population $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^N$ uniformly in $[\mathrm{lo},\mathrm{hi}]^d$, evaluate fitness.
2. For each generation, for each $i$: pick distinct $r_1\!\ne\!r_2\!\ne\!r_3\!\ne\!i$.
3. Mutation: $v = x_{r_1} + F\,(x_{r_2} - x_{r_3})$ with $F{=}0.5$.
4. Binomial crossover: $u_j = v_j$ if $\mathrm{rand}() < CR$ or $j = j_\text{rand}$, else $x_{i,j}$; $CR{=}0.9$.
5. Clip $u$ to bounds, evaluate.
6. Greedy selection: replace $x_i$ with $u$ iff $f(u) \le f(x_i)$.
diff_from_baseline: Storn & Price 1997 (Journal of Global Optimization). Canonical DE/rand/1/bin with Storn–Price recommended defaults.

name: GA + SBX
tagline: Real-coded genetic algorithm: tournament selection (k=3), Simulated Binary Crossover (η=20), polynomial bounded mutation.
pseudocode:
1. Initialize population uniformly in $[\mathrm{lo},\mathrm{hi}]^d$, evaluate fitness.
2. Selection: tournament of size $3$ → offspring (size N).
3. Crossover: with prob cx_prob apply SBX with $\eta_c{=}20$ to each pair.
4. Mutation: with prob mut_prob apply polynomial bounded mutation, $\eta_m{=}20$, indpb $= 1/d$.
5. Clip to bounds, evaluate invalid offspring.
6. Replace population with offspring; track best fitness per generation.
diff_from_baseline: Deb & Agrawal 1995 (Complex Systems). Standard real-coded GA used as a continuous-EA baseline; uses DEAP's `tools.cxSimulatedBinary` and `mutPolynomialBounded`.

name: L-SHADE
tagline: Adaptive DE with success-history F/CR memory, current-to-pbest/1 mutation with archive, and linear population size reduction.
pseudocode:
1. Init pop of $N_\text{init}$, history $M_F, M_{CR} = [0.5]^H$ ($H{=}6$), archive $A=\emptyset$.
2. For each $i$: sample $F_i\!\sim\!\mathrm{Cauchy}(M_F[r], 0.1)^+\!\le 1$, $CR_i\!\sim\!\mathcal{N}(M_{CR}[r], 0.1)$ clamped to $[0,1]$.
3. current-to-pbest/1 mutation with $p\!\in\![p_\min, 0.2]$ and external archive: $v = x_i + F_i(x_\text{pbest} - x_i) + F_i(x_{r1} - x_{r2})$.
4. Binomial crossover, clip, evaluate; greedy selection (improved trials enter pop, parents enter archive).
5. Update $M_F$ via weighted Lehmer mean of successful $F$, $M_{CR}$ via weighted arithmetic mean.
6. Linear population reduction: $N_{g+1} = N_\text{init} + (N_\min - N_\text{init})\frac{g+1}{G}$, prune worst.
diff_from_baseline: Tanabe & Fukunaga, IEEE CEC 2014. Strong adaptive DE family (variant of SHADE with linear pop-size reduction); routinely tops CEC competitions.

name: CMA-ES
tagline: Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy — adapts the full multivariate-Gaussian search distribution; SOTA derivative-free continuous optimizer.
pseudocode:
1. Initialize mean $m\!=\!\tfrac{\mathrm{lo}+\mathrm{hi}}{2}\mathbf{1}$, step size $\sigma\!=\!(\mathrm{hi}-\mathrm{lo})/3$, $C = I$, λ = pop_size.
2. Sample $x_k = m + \sigma\,\mathcal{N}(0, C)$, clip to bounds, evaluate.
3. Update mean by weighted recombination of top-$\mu$ samples.
4. Update evolution paths $p_\sigma, p_c$; rank-1 + rank-$\mu$ covariance update for $C$.
5. Update step size $\sigma$ via cumulative step-size adaptation (CSA).
6. Repeat for n_generations; track best-ever fitness.
diff_from_baseline: Hansen & Ostermeier 2001 (Evolutionary Computation). Default state-of-the-art ES for continuous black-box optimization; this baseline uses DEAP's `cma.Strategy`.
